quote_original: So he was called the one who brought the fish age.
context_before: Now we turn to a strange story in the Old Testament; one that very few priests and rabbis will be bold enough to mention from their pulpits. Here is one who is going to receive the promise as you now receive it. His name is Jesus, only the ancients called him Joshua, Jehoshua Ben Nun, or saviour, son of the fish, the Saviour of the great deep. Nun means fish, and fish is the element of the deep, the profound ocean. Jehoshua means Jehovah saves, and Ben means the offspring or son of.
context_after: This story is in the 6th book of the Bible, the book of Joshua. A promise is made to Joshua as it is made to Jesus in the Anglicized form in the gospe

quote_original: And when I reach that point the walls crumble.
context_before: Seven is a stillness, a rest, the Sabbath. It is the state when man is completely unmoved in his conviction that the thing is. When I can assume the feeling of my wish fulfilled and go to sleep, unconcerned, undisturbed, I am at rest mentally, and am keeping the Sabbath or am blowing the trumpet seven times.
context_after: Circumstances alter then remold themselves in harmony with my assumption. As they crumble I resurrect that which I have appropriated within. The walls, the obstacles, the problems, crumble of their own weight if I can reach the point of stillness within me.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 2 – Assumptions Harden Into Fact (1968-01-01).

quote_original: This golden cloud comes in meditation.
context_before: rmony with itself. The cloud is simply the garment of your consciousness, and where your consciousness is placed, there you will be in the flesh also.
context_after: There is a certain point when you are approaching sleep that it is very, very thick, very liquid, and very much alive and pulsing. It begins to ascend as you reach the drowsy, meditative state, bordering on sleep. You do not strike the tabernacle; neither do you move it until the cloud begins to ascend.

author: Neville Goddard

quote_original: Use wisely the interval preceding sleep.
context_before: night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed. Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction. ” Job 33: 15, 16
context_after: Assume the feeling of the wish fulfilled and go to sleep in this mood. At night, in a dimensionally larger world, when deep sleep falleth upon men, they see and play the parts that they will later on play on earth. And the drama is always in harmony with that which their dimensionally greater selves read and play through them. Our illusion of free will is but ignorance of the causes which make us act.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 2 – Assumptions Harden Into Fact (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: I sleep in that place now.
context_before: As my cloud ascends I assume that I am now the man I want to be, or that I am already in the place where I want to visit.
context_after: Then life strikes the tabernacle, strikes my environment and reassembles my environment across seas or over land and reassembles it in the likeness of my assumption. It has nothing to do with men walking across a physical desert. The whole vast world round about you is a desert.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 2 – Assumptions Harden Into Fact (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Why did they give you two days?
context_before: From the cradle to the grave you and I walk as though we walk the desert. But we have a living tabernacle wherein God dwells, and it is covered with a cloud which can and does ascend when we go to sleep or are in a state akin to sleep. Not necessarily in two days, it can ascend in two minutes.
context_after: If I now become the man I want to be, I may become dissatisfied tomorrow. I should at least give it a day before I decide to move on.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 2 – Assumptions Harden Into Fact (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Then repeat the phrase over and over like a lullaby.
context_before: When you have your phrase in mind, lift the cloud. Let the cloud ascend by simply inducing the state that borders on sleep. Simply begin to imagine and feel you are sleepy, and in this state assume the feeling of the wish fulfilled.
context_after: Whatever the phrase is, let it imply that the assumption is true, that it is concrete, that it is already a fact and you know it.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 2 – Assumptions Harden Into Fact (1968-01-01).
